summary: FidelityManager still lacks a no-execute boundary for caller-supplied PolicyConfig. On exact PR #274 head 60de91b49338249c1ded74db0d722921ce2fb55d, new(config) calls copyConfig(sourceConfig) before any raw-config shape check and evaluatePolicy validates config by dereferencing fields directly. A metatable-backed config can therefore execute __index during nominal data validation/copy. This is distinct from the already-active PolicyInputs numeric-scalar finding and should be consumed by the existing HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY primary rather than opening a competing source lane.
evidence: Exact PR #274 head 60de91b49338249c1ded74db0d722921ce2fb55d: validateConfig(config) dereferences config fields without first asserting a plain table with no metatable.
Exact PR #274 head 60de91b49338249c1ded74db0d722921ce2fb55d: FidelityManager.new(config) calls copyConfig(sourceConfig) before validateConfig, so hostile __index code can run before validation.

Exact PR #274 head 60de91b49338249c1ded74db0d722921ce2fb55d: evaluatePolicy(inputs, config, currentLevel) calls validateConfig(resolvedConfig), which also dereferences a caller-supplied config before a no-metatable guard.
Current Fidelity tests and the active PR #274 adversarial closure cover PolicyInputs no-execute behavior but do not contain an equivalent hostile PolicyConfig metatable regression.
